summary: Preinstall script downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs is obfuscated (hex-mangled identifiers, string-array indirection) and, on npm install, downloads a platform-specific Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts the bun binary to a temp directory, marks it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB obfuscated blob (mangled identifiers, large constant table, string-array rotation decoder of the shuffle-obfuscator family) marked '// @bun @bun-cjs', so it is only executable under the dropped Bun runtime and is not reachable by Node's module resolver or by Node-based scanners. The use of an alternate runtime specifically to execute an obfuscated sibling payload — combined with a package name that presents as a LaunchDarkly service wrapper — is a supply-chain attack pattern: installing the package causes arbitrary attacker-controlled code to run on the installer's machine at preinstall time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
